actions.resultDescription: The 'bane of all fish in the galaxy' were enjoying their leisure time when a gargantuan shadow passed beneath their air-filled boat. A true sea giant decided to respond in kind and attack the fishermen. Luckily, they managed to detect the attack in advance and escape the leviathan's hungry belly. Despite the scare, they do not seem to be discouraged from trying fishing in local waters again, already boasting of having caught quite a few impressive specimens.

nodes.name: Plant Diseases
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: The crew members working with the crops report that an unknown affliction is targeting the plants on the ship. Strange blue lines, like varicose veins, spread on the stalks, leaves, and roots. The afflicted plants continue to grow and develop as usual, but as they grow in size, those alien streaks stretch and spread further. Glowing. Pulsating. Upon examination, it appears to be a local parasitic lifeform that lives in the plants' endodermis. It is highly toxic and therefore unfit for consumption.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: It appears that some of the infected crops have wound up in the kitchen. Stomach aches, fever, and diarrhea are now the common afflictions among the crew.

penalties.name: Weakened Immunity I
penalties.comments: Affected cremember's Immunity is reduced by 40% (rounded up)

penalties.name: Weakened Health II
penalties.comments: The crew's HP maximum is reduced by a percentile. The missing amount of health is reduced first.

actions.description: The parasite that afflicts our plants is highly toxic. However, it is possible to reverse its fatal effects and use it for medical purposes.
actions.resultDescription: Your scientists work hard to turn the whole crisis upside down: from poison to cure. Eventually, they bring the good news: they have managed to extract the parasitic fluid from the plants and use it to create a batch of custom MedGel.

actions.description: The scientists are confident they can cure the affliction.
actions.resultDescription: Your scientists work hard on finding a way to neutralize the parasite's toxicity. Eventually, they bring the good news and inform you that, despite the lingering visual effects, the recently afflicted crops are fit for consumption.

actions.description: The compromised plant life is not suitable for consumption, but it can be processed into Chemical Fuel.
actions.resultDescription: The order is out, and the crew cuts down the blue-striped plants and hauls them to a workshop where they recycle them into Chemical Fuel.

nodes.name: Infestation
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: Distance from island less than 1, any building
nodes.spawnConditions: Distance from island less than 1, any building
nodes.eventDescription:
A gnarly, bulbous, black formation of alien origin appears in one of the buildings. The crew hears a low buzzing noise from inside. 
 The screams of the crew precede their appearance, running in panic from the building. The last man to get out closes the door and initiates a lockdown. When asked what happened, the crew tells about a strange black formation that appeared on the ceiling this morning. A gnarly, bulbous, tar-colored rock with porous walls spread and took over the facility, with a low buzzing noise humming inside. However, the mystery of that noise was short-lived. As the crew gaped at this unusual intrusion into their workspace, a bunch of amber-colored insects crawled out of that rock, spread their wings, and swooped toward the crew in what seemed to be a hostile maneuver.
The crew did not wait to find out and fled.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription:
The insects manage to find their way out of the locked-down building and attack the crew. Luckily, their stings cannot penetrate the safety suits and present no threat. A small number of wasps that have escaped are soon found and killed.
 It is not so easy to do with those in the nest inside the facility. As a result, the future shifts working there should spend some of their time fighting off the annoying insects.

penalties.comments: Buildings' or crew's  productivity is reduced by 80 for duration fo effect.

actions.description: Create a chemical poison and kill the uninvited guests.

You send a group equipped with improvised spraying devices to disperse the chemical poison. It works like a charm, quickly killing the insects.
 After that, all that is left to be done is to remove the nest formation.

actions.description: Burn the nest, ignoring all the damage done to the building in the process.
actions.resultDescription: You send a group equipped with improvised flamethrowers to shoot fire at the insects and their nest. As expected, these bugs are no more resistant to fire than their distant relatives back on Earth.  Unfortunately, during this mission, the building itself caught fire. And so, after the fight against insects was over, the fight against fire began.

rewards.name: Boosted Productivity II

nodes.name: Special Training
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: in the open sea, Game stage 2 or more, Behemoth
nodes.spawnConditions: in the open sea, Game stage 2 or more, Behemoth
nodes.eventDescription:
Orest Demchuck, Security Force Commanding Officer, wants to lead a special training course on survival for the crew.
Your head of scouts is adamant about the necessity of such training. "Do I really need to explain the benefits of survival skills? We are on an alien planet with a thousand elaborate ways to kill us. How to defend oneself, how to patch up your wounded crew member, how to make fire out of mud and sticks, how to navigate by stars, how to… I mean, the list can go on. All these how-tos can tip the scales between life and death in the former's favor. And give us another day to make something out of the situation we are in."

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The training course remains a missed opportunity.

actions.description: Allow Orest to organize a self-defense training course.
actions.resultDescription: The crew undergoes a series of vigorous exercises: close combat, accuracy shooting, obstacle course traversal, and many others. The muscles throb and ache, making the next day of work a more tiring experience, but the skills learned and the knowledge gained are invaluable.

actions.description: Every crew member must know how to provide first aid.
actions.resultDescription: The crew learns several applications of MedGel and the basics of first aid. How to stop bleeding, what to do when a heart stops, and even less extreme situations, like what to do when someone faints, are given much-needed time, so that the crew can be ready for any exigency.

rewards.comments: The crew's HP maximum is increased by a percentile. The extra HP max comes filled with extra health.

actions.description: It is important to know how to navigate freighters, recon crafts, and the ship itself.
actions.resultDescription: The crew learns how to navigate various types of available vessels and how to interpret sensor readings to avoid unwanted collisions on the island-riddled planet.

actions.description: If stranded on the island, people should know how to craft basics, how to use available tools, and how to fix broken equipment.
actions.resultDescription: Orest invites Tuuli, the Chief Engineer, to give a masterclass on survival crafting. It starts with basics, such as making a lean-to and starting a fire, and then the training gets progressively more complicated as Tuuli forces crew members to disassemble various tools and gadgets to learn how to repair them.

nodes.eventDescription:
The Medbay has been developing a special vaccine meant to boost the crew's immunity to the local pathogens.
 The crew of Behemoth is alien to this planet, and the risk of someone catching some indigenous virus or bacteria is always present. Surely, the crew follows a set of strict rules and precautions to reduce the chance of contracting a deadly strain, but it would be much better for the crew to have resistance to the unwanted gifts of this planet. To create a vaccine, the doctors need to study one of the following subjects extensively.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: You ignored requests from the team. The “Nocebo effect” caused by continuous stress among team members regarding potential alien sickness actually worsened their natural resistance.

nodes.spawnConditions: Game stage 3 or more, morale less then 50, Behemoth
nodes.eventDescription:
A crew member tried to jump over the safety rail and disappear into the water. 
 A severely depressed individual, who attempted a one-way dive into the water, has been admitted to the health center. At first, the man is taciturn when questioned about his well-being. Later, he expresses his unwillingness to continue with this 'farce.' "It is all pointless," he says. "He is right. The sooner it ends, the better." He does not explain who is right...
This man is not alone in his misery. Lately, the halls are full of dark, despondent whispers. And there seems to be someone responsible for the spread of this despair... You hear rumors of a ghost, of a lonely voice echoing in the halls.

But this AI agent is the one spreading disturbing ideas and sowing seeds of doubt in the minds of your crew.  The AI core is removed. And the mysterious ghost is no more.

Unless this is resolved, our coordination will continue to unravel and productivity will decline further. I recommend swiftly standardizing procedures and clarifying protocols to restore order.
With due respect, Mnemosyne."

nodes.name: Stowaway Fauna
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: Distance from island less than 1, Target: Behemoth
nodes.spawnConditions: Distance from island less than 1, Target: Behemoth
nodes.eventDescription: Several specimens of the local fauna hitched a ride on one of the cargo ships and weren't discovered until they had already established a small colony in the less-visited parts of the Behemoth. They appear harmless, they're cute, and the crew loves having them around — someone started calling them Plumplins, and the name stuck.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The colony works its way into new vents and any corner nobody checks. Cleanup is no longer a quick job.

penalties.name: Waste Issues II
penalties.comments: Each affected building produces 50% more waste.

actions.description: Fence off a small habitat, run regular sanitation checks, and keep the colony under observation.
actions.resultDescription: The crew adopts the Plumplins as unofficial mascots. Spirits lift, and medbay reports a measurable boost to crew immunity. The only cost is a slight dip in productivity — people keep finding reasons to walk past the habitat.

rewards.name: Boosted Immunity I
rewards.comments: Affected cremember's Immunity is Increased by 50% (rounded up)

rewards.name: Morale Boost I
rewards.comments: The crewmember's morale is increased by 10 for that duration (can surpass 100)

rewards.name: Productivity Slowdown I
rewards.comments: Buildings' or crew's  productivity is reduced by 20 for duration fo effect.

actions.description: A xenofauna colony aboard is not something we can sign off on. Crate the animals carefully and keep them safe until we reach a suitable island.
actions.resultDescription: Nobody wanted to be the one who hurt them. The nest came out in one piece — lined material, scraps, and all — and went straight into a crate padded for the trip. The Plumplins moved in after it without much fuss, and the crew spent the rest of the shift checking on them.

actions.description: Nothing from this planet has been cleared for life aboard, harmless or not. Euthanize the specimens under bio-protocol and forward samples to the lab.
actions.resultDescription: The crew took it badly. Something settled over the ship afterwards that nobody puts into words. The researchers logged an anomalous organic artifact recovered from the nest, along with a strange connection to the Plumplins themselves.

nodes.name: Pest Problem
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location:
in the open sea, Specific building, Bioengineering
Workshop, Universum, Plantation, Farm
nodes.spawnConditions:
in the open sea, Specific building, Bioengineering
Workshop, Universum, Plantation, Farm
nodes.eventDescription: A unique pest problem has disrupted operations—if something resembling a shark with legs can be called a pest. The creature somehow squeezed into the food production buildings, leaving chaos and a mess in its wake. Now, it falls to the crew to devise a solution for handling this unusual intruder.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Without intervention, the legged shark continues to roam freely, creating ongoing disorder and causing mounting frustration among the crew tasked with food production. Morale takes a hit as the nuisance persists.

actions.description: Observe the locations where the creature appears most often and carefully prepare a humane trap to capture it without harm.
actions.resultDescription: The "pest" turns out to be a secret pet belonging to one of the crew. After it was finally cornered, the ambush turned into something closer to a celebration: everyone took turns getting a look at it, the owner got their share of jokes, and then the creature was quietly released.

actions.description: Closely monitor the creature’s movement patterns to determine how it enters the building and uncover its origins.
actions.resultDescription: Tailing the creature reveals its true nature — a secret pet kept by one of the crew. The owner admits what he'd been doing, and after a short goodbye the creature goes back into the wild. The patrol turns out to be a welcome break for everyone involved: a bit of movement, a bit of fresh air, and the whole group comes back looser and more awake.

actions.description: Review and strengthen the building’s security protocols, eliminating any loopholes that allowed the “shark” to gain access.
actions.resultDescription: Once new protocols are in place, the creature’s secret owner has no choice but to come forward and admit the truth. The pet is released safely into the wild. The tightened security standards prompt the crew to work diligently to adapt, boosting overall discipline and work ethic.

nodes.name: Lets Go Gambling
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: What started as a harmless way to kill time has spiraled into a full-blown craze aboard the ship. Crew members now collect bacteria-like cultures in petri dishes and place bets on which sample will flourish first - turning the pastime into a racing league. Although the activity seems innocent enough, concerns are growing that it could easily lead to a serious accident.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: As anticipated, one of the extremophile bacteria escapes containment, rapidly corroding part of the ship’s structure. The incident serves as a costly reminder of the dangers unchecked fun can unleash.

penalties.name: Corrosive Mold
penalties.comments: Each hour, affected building loses 5 points of Integrity.

actions.description: Provide specialized equipment to ensure each “race” is safely contained, along with education on disease prevention to minimize health risks.
actions.resultDescription: With improved containment gear and briefings on the dangers of improper handling, the crew’s competitions become much safer. Not only is the risk of disease spread drastically reduced, but the heightened awareness gives everyone’s immunity a welcome boost.

actions.description: Introduce precision tools and encourage the crew to reinvent the contest, using their enthusiasm to cultivate new antibiotics instead of hazards.
actions.resultDescription: With upgraded tools and a new purpose, the crew channels their competitive energy into real research. Friendly rivalries now push them to discover promising antibiotic candidates, blending fun with meaningful contributions to shipwide health.

actions.description: Impose immediate restrictions and dismantle the competition to prevent any risk of an outbreak.
actions.resultDescription: Though some crew members are disappointed, the swift action pays off — potential threats are neutralized before they can develop, safeguarding the entire vessel from a possible epidemic. Fortunately, a few of the cell cultures are salvaged safely and can be repurposed as basic medicine, providing a small but valuable benefit to the ship’s medical reserves.

nodes.name: Birthday Party
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: A rumor has started to circulate across the ship: Executive Officer Khalil Arida may be celebrating his birthday soon. Though he has always been guarded about such personal matters, some say the old man deserves a little festivity in his honor. Perhaps it’s time to show some appreciation — whether he admits to the occasion or not.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The supposed birthday passes with no celebration or gift. Later, word spreads that Khalil’s birthday was actually on another day. Some crew members feel a twinge of disappointment, wondering if their own special days might someday be forgotten as well, leaving the atmosphere a bit subdued.

actions.description: Invite a few crew members to help plan and organize a surprise birthday celebration for Khalil.
actions.resultDescription: The crew gathers in the R&D lab, ready with decorations and homemade treats to greet the officer. Throughout the party, Khalil appears pleasantly surprised, though a bit bewildered by all the fuss. At the end, he quietly confides that today isn’t actually his birthday. Nevertheless, the crew enjoys themselves immensely, and the shared laughter brings everyone a little closer together.

actions.description: Recruit personnel to craft a thoughtful and practical gift for Khalil — something he’d truly appreciate.
actions.resultDescription: Pooling their skills, the team assembles a fresh powercell, recalling that Khalil’s equipment has been in need of an upgrade. When the gift is presented privately, Khalil politely declines, explaining that his birthday isn’t today. Even so, the spare powercell finds a grateful home aboard the ship, proving useful for the entire crew.

nodes.name: Birds and Bees
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location:
Game stage 2 or later
at least 1 crabari crew member, in the open sea
nodes.spawnConditions:
Game stage 2 or later
at least 1 crabari crew member, in the open sea
nodes.eventDescription: A human crew member has been sharing some deep connection with Ruthless-Sky (short Ruth), a crabari hired on deck. The crewmember finds Ruth's powerful stature and kind eyes incredibly attractive, and Ruth sees crewmember's "clan" (the rest of vessel's crew) strong enough for him to be a feasible mate. Despite cultural differences between humans and crabari, they want to play wedding.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Disheartened by the lack of response from the captain, Ruthless-Sky and the unnamed crew member decided to take matters into their own hands. Under the cover of night, the pair slipped away from the ship, climbing atop a mysterious marine creature that surfaced near the hull. By morning, both were gone without a trace.  Little is known of their whereabouts, yet hope remains among the crew that, wherever they are, the unlikely couple has found happiness together.

actions.description: Organize a generous meal for the newlyweds and all interested crew, ensuring plenty of food to fuel the festivities and foster unity.
actions.resultDescription: The wedding feast turned out to be wonderfully lavish, even with limited resources. Bellies were so full by the end that several crew members vowed to start a diet immediately afterward.

rewards.name: Fasting
rewards.effect: each food charge lasts 4 hours for 24 hours
rewards.comments: The crewmember spends each food charge every 4 hours, while receiving effects of food every hour as usual.

actions.description: Create a festive atmosphere with makeshift fireworks, launching a salute to honor the union and bring a vibrant sense of celebration to the deck.
actions.resultDescription: The ceremony was simple, set amid the practical backdrop of the R&D lab, with rings fashioned from scrap metal. As the two exchanged vows and became a couple, the ship seemed just a little warmer. Word of the union spread, and sympathetic traders across the sector offered financial gifts to celebrate the new couple’s happiness.

rewards.name: Delighted Crabari Traders
rewards.comments: Buying prices are reduced by 30% (rounded up) for the trader of that Crabari.

actions.description: Bring together a few crew members for a thoughtful discussion with the couple — love is powerful, but it may be wise to consider if they’re moving too quickly.
actions.resultDescription: The candid discussion led by crew experts went smoothly. Ruth and the crew member agreed they’d jumped in too quickly and decided to remain friends — for now. As they exited, an officer swears the crew member gave Ruth a sly wink, hinting that the story might not be over just yet.

rewards.name: Morale Stasis
rewards.comments: Morale value is frozen at the level it was when status effect has started. This effect can be overridden by bonus and debuff to morale effects.

nodes.name: Energy Leaks
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: Game stage 3 or more, in the open sea, any energy building
nodes.spawnConditions: Game stage 3 or more, in the open sea, any energy building
nodes.eventDescription: We detected odd voltage spikes on the power lines, and tracing them led us to an unexpected visitor. Some kind of creature has made itself at home in the power conduits. As far as we can tell, it's eating our electricity.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Undisturbed, the creature resumed drawing energy from the source. The crew were not impressed by their commander's helplessness.

actions.description: To get rid of the creature, we need to be creative. If it feeds on energy, we'll build a lure and draw it back into the ocean. There's some risk involved, but we'll manage.
actions.resultDescription: The operation was largely a success. The creature pounced on the bait without hesitation. That said, a few crew members were injured while installing the lure and in the aftermath. Still, it was spectacular, so morale is up.

actions.description: We cannot allow this creature to threaten the crew and cripple our power supply. Prepare the team to eliminate it.
actions.resultDescription: After the creature was attacked, it emitted a a powerful signal. It appears to have been a call for help, so be ready for a potential threat from the depths.

actions.description: It is too risky to interact with the creature directly. Send researchers with the right gear to study it from a safe distance.
actions.resultDescription: Studies of the creature have revealed extraordinary properties in its internal organs: they consume, store, and convert energy with remarkable efficiency. The research has since given rise to the idea of a new Energy Building.

nodes.name: Allergy Season
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: During the shift, a commonly used reagent in production was found to act as an irritant, leading several crew members to develop allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing, itching, and watery eyes. The affected crew members report discomfort, and production pace slows as safety checks and substitutions are considered.

inactionThreat.description: No solution, everyone sneezing
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The effects of the irritant intensified, and symptoms escalated into widespread malaise. The crew is left feeling unwell and uncomfortable, with persistent itching affecting everyone.

penalties.name: Weakened Health II
penalties.comments: The crew's HP maximum is reduced by a percentile. The missing amount of health is reduced first.

actions.description: Prepare and distribute a suitable remedy to relieve crew members’ irritation symptoms.
actions.resultDescription: The remedy proved highly effective among the crew, not only alleviating irritation symptoms but also providing a noticeable boost to overall well-being.

rewards.name: Health Recovery
rewards.effect: gain 5 HP per hour for 48 hours
rewards.comments: Affected crewmembers regain missing HP at the rate of 5HP per hour.

actions.description: Inspect and replace air filters in the affected factory area to reduce exposure to the irritant.
actions.resultDescription: Inspection revealed that faulty filters were the source of the problem. With repairs completed, crew symptoms have drastically diminished, and as an added benefit, the risk of disease transmission has been reduced.

rewards.name: Boosted Immunity I
rewards.comments: Affected cremember's Immunity is Increased by 50% (rounded up)

actions.description: Provide proper containers so the crew can safely collect, inspect, and research the irritant to develop an effective solution.
actions.resultDescription: The crew successfully adjusted the reagent formula to lessen its irritating effects. Additionally, several members gained valuable hands-on experience, leading to new specializations within the team.

nodes.name: Light Backlog
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: For the first time in days the board is clean and pressure is low. Tools are staged, crews are on shift, and we have a short window to either pull work forward, invest in people, or clear the small blockers that usually slow the first hour of a surge.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The lull passes without a plan. Although everything seems fine now, the first hour of the next surge is slowed by missing approvals, labels, and tool checks that could have been addressed earlier. The crew face the same friction as before, and the chance to build momentum is missed.

penalties.name: Productivity Slowdown I
penalties.comments: Buildings' or crew's  productivity is reduced by 20 for duration fo effect.

actions.description: Use spare time to plan for the next rush, ensuring maximum efficiency.
actions.resultDescription: The crew have planned out the next hours and are now able to address upcoming situations more efficiently, resulting in a spike in overall productivity.

rewards.name: Boosted Productivity II
rewards.comments: Buildings' or crew's productivity is increased by 50 for duration fo effect.

actions.description: Use available time to run a group workshop focused on long-term crew preparedness.
actions.resultDescription: Some crew members used this time to deepen their understanding of logistics, becoming more specialized in their roles and enabling smoother, more efficient task execution for everyone.

nodes.name: Stowaway Fauna
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventIntro: This place seems perfect for releasing the Plumplins. Take a closer look at it first.
nodes.eventDescription: Although our knowledge of these owl-like creatures is limited, observations suggest the island has everything they need. We can send a team ashore to find the right spot and help them settle in.

actions.description: Survey the island for the best spot, release the Plumplins there, and stay long enough to see how they settle.
actions.resultDescription: The Plumplins took to the prepared nesting site at once and settled in, healthy and content. Over the following days they grew attached to the crew, and when it came time to part ways, they left something from the nest behind. The crew chose to read it as a thank-you.

actions.description: Release the Plumplins on the island and leave them to it — the habitat looks safe, and they'll adapt.
actions.resultDescription: With bittersweet emotions, the crew released the adorable creatures into the wild, confident that the island will provide them a new home. Though farewells were teary, the crew felt joy knowing the Plumplins were safe and free, ready to embrace their new life.

nodes.name: Hangar Deck Fire Drill
nodes.eventIntro: Sirens blare across the lower catwalks as simulated thermal alarms trip.
nodes.eventDescription: Chief Engineer orders an unannounced high-readiness damage control drill.

inactionThreat.description: No team responded in time.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Penalty applied.

actions.description: Direct crew to seal airlocks and foam containment.
actions.resultDescription: Hangar secured ahead of schedule.

nodes.title: Hangar Deck Fire Drill

nodes.name: Ancient AI Core
nodes.eventIntro: The interior atmospheric sensors flicker to life. A faint cybernetic hum resonates through the bulkhead.
nodes.eventDescription: Deep within the sunken vessel, a dormant intelligence awakens.

actions.description: Interface directly with the terminal.
actions.resultDescription: Data extracted successfully.

nodes.name: Field Research
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: spawn on Biome 01, Biome 06, Biome 10 = shallow any island
nodes.spawnConditions: spawn on Biome 01, Biome 06, Biome 10 = shallow any island
nodes.eventIntro: Your scouts find a lot of animals' carcasses. Studying them could be useful.
nodes.eventDescription: While exploring the island, your scouts discover a group of dead and dying land animals scattered along the shore. They are apparently struck by an unknown disease. Examining them could help you learn more about local viruses or toxins.

actions.description: Extract Tissue
actions.resultDescription: Your scouts thoroughly examined the animal carcasses and collected  samples from both diseased and apparently healthy organs and tissues. These samples will improve your understanding of the local fauna.

actions.description: Neutralise the virus
actions.resultDescription: Your scouts thoroughly examined the animal carcasses and collected samples from both diseased and apparently healthy organs and tissues. After further research and adjustments to the medical lab, the scouts reported that the virus had been neutralized and no longer posed a threat to humans or your food supplies.

actions.description: Reverse the sickness
actions.resultDescription: Your scouts thoroughly examined the animal carcasses and collected samples from both diseased and apparently healthy organs and tissues. After further research and adjustments to the medical lab, they developed a custom batch of MedGel that not only neutralized the virus but also reversed its effects, saving several creatures on the brink of death.

nodes.name: Supply Beacon
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventIntro: A supply beacon has crashed. Something inside might still be useful.
nodes.eventDescription: The supply beacon has crashed into the island and turned into a jumble of metal. Whatever contents it transported must have been smashed into smithereens and less. And yet, with proper tools, your specialists may be able to salvage something.

actions.resultDescription: Your specialists cut through the damaged hull and recovered the cargo stored inside. The salvaged supplies  have been added to your stockpile.
Your specialists dismantled the beacon and sorted the wreckage, recovering reusable  materials.
Your specialists carefully removed the surviving electronics from the beacon's hull, recovering useful components.

nodes.name: Distress Call
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventIntro: A wrecked escape pod is on fire. There may be survivors inside.
nodes.eventDescription: The escape pod must have crashed into the island with high enough speed, given its battered appearance. What is worse — it is now on fire. Your people start shouting to identify if there are survivors inside.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Crew members challenged your decision, arguing that saving lives was a fundamental human duty. Your order not to intervene sparked prolonged debates in the crew quarters, lowering morale.

actions.resultDescription: Your specialists picked the lock, but wiring, damaged while pod had crushed, electrified the capsules hull. One crew member suffered an electric shock during the operation. However all three survivors were rescued and joined your crew, boosting morale.

Your specialists slowly melted  through the lock. The air pressure between an airlock and outside the capsule equilized, allowing them to open the door safely. All three survivors were rescued and joined your crew, boosting morale.

Your specialists forced the pod open with a crafted lever. The  pressure difference between a hatch and the outside  caused explosive decompression. All three survivors were injured  as well as one of your crew. But all survivors were rescued and joined your crew, boosting morale.

nodes.name: Cave system
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: During a scouting expedition along the shore, a crew member hears a strange metallic sound amid the waves. Following it, the scouts discover a cave entrance exposed by low tide. Waves rock pieces of metal debris in the shallows, making them clang together. Inside, passages lead to a larger cave network. With the tide rising, the crew debates whether exploring further is worth the time and risk.

actions.description: Action description...
actions.resultDescription: Using scanners, the scouts trace the anomalies to an artifact inside the first chamber. The rising tide leaves little time to retrieve it. While retrieving the artifact, the crew discovers a passage to a deeper cave network. But time spent debating and scanning allows the rising tide to cut off access, preventing further exploration.

actions.description: Description for action choice B...
actions.resultDescription: A thorough inspection reveals a rich metal ore vein extending into a deeper cave network. With the tide rising, the crew chooses to extract what ore they can rather than explore further.

actions.description: Description for action choice C...
actions.resultDescription: Deeper in the caves, the scouts find a row of doors on the wall, each smaller than the last. None leads anywhere, painted. An air analyzer detects traces of incense used by Nasobi. Some crew members see an impressive artistic statement of one of Nasobies' artists; others see a waste of time. They debate modern art on the way back, but crew morale remains unchanged.

nodes.name: Field Research 2
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: spawn on Biome 01, Biome 06, Biome 10 = shallow
nodes.spawnConditions: spawn on Biome 01, Biome 06, Biome 10 = shallow
nodes.eventDescription: The scouts discover strange plants growing in neat rows across a patch of warm ground. They collect promising samples, but when one scout pulls at a root, the entire patch rises beneath their feet. Their garden is growing on the back of a huge beasts, luying in a pack and it is now awake.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The crew slowly backs away, hoping the beasts will lose interest. Instead, the animals begin to surround them, showing coordinated hunting behavior. Two crew members are killed before the others can escape.

actions.description: Action description...
actions.resultDescription: The scouts shield themselves from the enraged beasts. During the confrontation, the equipment becomes coated in mucus secreted by the creatures. Analysis of the substance reveals how the beasts resist local infections, allowing the crew to improve their own defenses against native diseases.

actions.description: Description for action choice B...
actions.resultDescription: The scouts scares the beasts away, and collect promising samples of metals and algae from their resting place before making a hasty retreat. Further analysis of the samples improves the crew’s understanding of local viruses.

actions.description: Description for action choice C...
actions.resultDescription: The scouts attack the beasts, but the bullets fail to pierce their thick hides, merely driving them away and leaving no bodies to examine. However, the crew collects promising samples of metals and algae from their resting place. Further analysis of the biological samples improves their understanding of local viruses.

nodes.name: Field Research
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.location: spawn on Biome 01, Biome 06, Biome 10 = shallow
nodes.spawnConditions: spawn on Biome 01, Biome 06, Biome 10 = shallow
nodes.eventDescription: The scouts collect tissue samples from huge mollusk-like creatures in the tidal pools—a promising source of protein. Nearby, they find piles of shattered shells. One scout blames the surf; another points out that every shell is broken on the same side. Something here has a bigger appetite. As the crew packs up, a large beast emerges from behind the rocks and growls. They have been sampling its food.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Crew members challenged your decision, arguing that saving lives was a fundamental human duty. Your order not to intervene sparked prolonged debates in the crew quarters, lowering morale.

actions.description: Action description...
actions.resultDescription: The crew attacks first, but the beast’s thick hide prevents a fatal hit. Wounded, it flees. The fight gives the scouts valuable combat experience, and they return more confident in their ability to defend themselves against the local fauna.

actions.description: Description for action choice B...
actions.resultDescription: A blast sends the beast fleeing behind the rocks and exposes mineral deposits beneath the shattered surface. The crew collects samples before making a hasty retreat. Everyone agrees the samples are not worth risking their lives for.

actions.description: Description for action choice C...
actions.resultDescription: The crew tosses out bait. While the beast sniffs the unfamiliar food, they shoot it with a sample collection capsule. Startled, it flees, leaving behind a sample of its remarkably tough skin. Everyone agrees the samples are not worth risking their lives for and retreats.

nodes.name: The Ferals
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: The scouts see smoke in the distance, as if from a bonfire. They head toward that smoke when they are attacked by a group of men, humans. One of the scouts is grievously wounded. All attempts to reach out and communicate with the attackers are ignored. All they want is to spill the blood of your people; their hearts are full of murderous zeal.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Crew members challenged your decision, arguing that saving lives was a fundamental human duty. Your order not to intervene sparked prolonged debates in the crew quarters, lowering morale.

actions.description: Action description...
actions.resultDescription: The crew fights back, killing some of the attackers and forcing the rest to fall back temporarily. Still outnumbered, the scouts use the opening to retreat. Later, a review of the expedition recordings reveals growths covering the attackers’ faces and damage to their suits. The crew suspects a local virus entered through the breaches and affected their brains, causing aggression similar to rabies, an ancient Earth disease.

actions.description: Description for action choice B...
actions.resultDescription: There are too many attackers, and the crew is reluctant to hurt fellow humans. They decide to retreat quickly. Later, a review of the expedition recordings reveals growths covering the attackers’ faces and damage to their suits. The crew suspects a local virus entered through the breaches and affected their brains, causing aggression similar to rabies, an ancient Earth disease.

actions.description: Description for action choice C...
actions.resultDescription: Outnumbered, the crew avoids close combat and calls in artillery fire to drive the attackers back. As they flee, they abandon several useful items, which the scouts collect as spoils. Later, a review of the expedition recordings reveals growths covering the attackers’ faces and damage to their suits. The crew suspects a local virus entered through the breaches and affected their brains, causing aggression similar to rabies, an ancient Earth disease.

nodes.name: Anomaly
nodes.title: New Event Block
nodes.eventDescription: Once above the island, the scouts fly their recon craft into the most dangerous airspace they have ever flown through. The sky appears to be littered with balls of lightning, unseen until you fly too close to them.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: The scouts decide to land and wait out the storm. Ten minutes later, an enormous lightning bolt strikes the island, cutting off all communication with the team. Even after the storm subsides, contact cannot be restored. A rescue team is dispatched to investigate, but finds nothing at the landing site except a pool of molten metal where the recon craft once stood.

actions.description: Use the Basic Extractor to absorb the electrical energy and clear a path through the storm.
actions.resultDescription: As the device begins drawing in the discharges, the glowing spheres flicker and gradually dissipate. After several tense minutes, they manage to clear a narrow passage through the storm. The recon craft escapes the dangerous airspace and safely returns to the ship.

actions.description: Use specialized equipment to investigate the source of the lightning.
actions.resultDescription: The scouts attempt to locate the center of the storm and fly as far away from it as possible, carefully maneuvering between the lightning balls. After several tense minutes, the lightning becomes less frequent, and the recon craft eventually escapes the storm and returns safely to the ship.

actions.description: Fire metal projectiles to divert the lightning away from the recon craft.
actions.resultDescription: The plan works: electrical discharges strike the projectiles, briefly clearing a path through the storm. Taking advantage of the opening, the crew maneuvers through the remaining lightning balls and safely returns to the ship.

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventDescription: The likelihood of anyone surviving the spaceship's destruction is low but not zero: Zephyrus had self-propelled emergency escape pods and shuttles distributed throughout the ship for evacuation. Someone could have reached them just in time. But what exactly could destroy Zephyrus, our most advanced and well-protected spaceship? Could the Behemoth be next? Learning more about what happened might increase the chances of survival for this ship and its crew. For that, the flight recorder and the bridge voice recorder must be retrieved.

actions.description: Harsh conditions jam the long-distance signals. To pick up the emergency signal from the escape pods, a more powerful transmitter is required.
actions.resultDescription: The transmitter has picked up several signals, all heavily distorted. For now, it is unclear whether any of them belong to an escape pod, but Mnemosyne will work on finding out.

actions.description: Mnemosyne can analyze all the recorded data of the Zephyrus's destruction and predict the probable crash sites of its debris, including the pieces where the flight recorders should be contained.
actions.resultDescription: Mnemosyne is about to determine a possible crash site area of the mothership's fragment containing the Orange box. The fragment is still in orbit and has yet to pass through the lower atmosphere, shattering in the process and thus complicating the precise prediction of the orange box's final location.

nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.spawnConditions: On an island with additional escape pod model.
nodes.eventIntro: An escape pod must be somewhere on this island, as this is where its distress signal is coming from.
nodes.eventDescription: Blood, claw marks, shredded EVAs, guts, torn limbs, and more blood greet your scouts inside the escape pod. Something has gotten to the space refugees before you.

inactionThreat.description: Event times out without choice made.
inactionThreat.resultDescription: Catastrophic failure occurs due to delay.

actions.description: Arm the scouts and send them to search the island for survivors (or their bodies).
actions.resultDescription:
The escape shuttle's log accounts for six passengers, one of them a child. The cameras show that two passengers of the shuttle had died before the creatures attacked. They bled from their eyes and were delirious.

In the end, they grew aggressive and forced other passengers to flee.       

The wild beasts only ravaged the corpses and did not attack any other member of the evacuation.       

That's when the scouts notice the last clue. Each escape shuttle, specifically designed for Keeling in mind, is equipped with a lifeboat in case the landing happens to be 'watering.' And such a lifeboat is currently missing from the shuttle's inventory.

actions.description: Investigate the scene to gather clues, recreate the events, and learn more about the fate of the survivors.
actions.resultDescription:
Despite the lack of progress in locating people from Zephyrus, the scouts have had significant success in finding the predators, possibly responsible for attacking the escape shuttle. All they had to do was stay on the island long enough to become bait for the hungry beasts.

The ambush left two of the party severely wounded, but the team managed to fight off and retreat to the extraction point, leaving the island without discovering the fate of the survivors.

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: According to Mnemosyne's predictions, the section of the mothership containing the orange box should have landed on this island.
nodes.eventDescription:
The scouts follow the column of smoke that echoes the trajectory of the fallen fragment. The closer they get, the more destruction they see. The blast from the impact has melted stone and banished the living elements from the location. Not a blade of grass has remained. Just pockmarks from stone-turned-shrapnel everywhere, leaving long-standing scars.
 And then, a crater. A large, smoldering chunk of twisted metal lies inside. The dispatched scouts approach a burial ground of their mothership, watching it somberly — another reminder of what they have lost.

actions.description: Six hours of painstaking and careful "surgery" are required to extract the orange box without any risk of damaging it.
actions.resultDescription:
Slowly and carefully, like handling a bomb that is one wrong move away from detonating, the team peels off layer after layer of metal, exposing a mess of fried spaceship's innards. In the process, they manage to salvage quite a few valuable parts and components that can be useful for our survival.

Finally, after long hours of exhausting dissection, the flight data recorder is retrieved. It appears to be intact.

actions.description: We have no time to waste on the surgical dissection. We need the orange box, and we need it ASAP.
actions.resultDescription:
Tuuli, Chief Engineer, does her best to calculate the amount of explosive charges, as well as their placement, to keep the further destruction of Zephyrus's wreck under control. Despite her best efforts, all the fine elements of the spaceship that could have survived the fall are now beyond salvation.

The flight data recorder appears to have taken serious damage, too. Its integrity is compromised. It is unclear whether your team's explosive extraction techniques are to blame, but it is doubtful they have improved the situation.

nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: Repelled by the overwhelming numbers of local predators, the scouts failed to discover the fate of the survivors. It is the time to learn from our mistakes and attempt again.
nodes.eventDescription: The island is swarming with dangerous predators. And somewhere, surrounded by violent beasts, a group of survivors might still be alive. Or so many of your crew want to believe.

actions.description: Protected by force shields, an armed group can easily dispatch the hunting packs of predators and provide the necessary aid to survivors if any are found.
actions.resultDescription: The scouts move swiftly through the island, unhindered. Claws and fangs fail to pierce the force fields encompassing the bodies of the scouts, while the bullets find no such problem with the animal hides.  But all that bloodshed leads to nothing. Your scouts find no survivors on the island, nor their remains.  But when they pass by the escape pod one more time, they realize that it does not have the emergency lifeboat. And since animals don't usually sail on boats, it can mean only one thing...

actions.description: The drones should not attract the unwanted attention of local predators and will therefore traverse the island more efficiently.
actions.resultDescription:
As expected, the drones are of no interest to the carnivores and pass through the island without a hitch. But after hours of circling around, they find no evidence of any human being present in this place.

Eventually, passing by the escape pod one more time, one of the operators notices that a lifeboat is missing. And since animals don't usually sail on boats, it can mean only one thing...

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: The lifeboat is feverishly tossed around by the legion of turbulent waves.
nodes.eventDescription: Your scouts reach the lifeboat and meet the survivors. But it is not the reunion they have been hoping for.  People on the lifeboat look horrible. Their eyes bulge in pain, rimmed by blood. Crimson tears run down and spread, like Martian deltas, on their puffed, inflamed faces.

actions.description: Bring the survivors to the ship and provide them with all the necessary medical help.
actions.resultDescription:
The scouts return with the blood-crying survivors, and the fight for their lives begins.

Based on the preliminary examination, the virus appears to be a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It is much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More work needs to be done to better understand its properties, learn how it ended up on Keeling, and find a way to treat it.

actions.description: Keep the survivors on the lifeboat and examine the virus there, thus avoiding any unnecessary risks for the crew on the Behemoth.
actions.resultDescription: R&D scientists and doctors give instructions to the scouts. They examine the survivors, collect the samples for R&D analysis, and do what they can to help. In the end, nothing works, and the scouts give the final gift to the tormented people — painkillers.  Having taken all the necessary precautions, the scouts then deliver the samples to the R&D lab for further research.  The virus appears to be a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It is much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More research is needed to better understand its properties and how it ended up on Keeling.

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: The lifeboat is tossed around by the legion of turbulent waves. Radio silence greets your ship.
nodes.eventDescription:
Bodies of the survivors, who are survivors no more, cover the floor of the lifeboat's only cabin. Their eyes bulge in pain, rimmed by a dried moat of blood. Crimson tears have run down and spread, like Martian deltas, on their puffed, still inflamed faces. These people have fled from horrible death in space and on the island, only to succumb to a no less cruel disease.  Among those corpses also lies the frail body of a child.

It is not Liora.

actions.description: Send scouts to take the samples for the R&D lab.
actions.resultDescription: Having taken all the necessary precautions, the scouts extract the samples and deliver them to the R&D lab for further research. Mars Abbadie, the Head of R&D, contacts you later with preliminary results. The virus is a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It is much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More research is needed to better understand its properties and how it ended up on Keeling.

actions.description: The examination must be conducted remotely using drones.
actions.resultDescription: Transmitted results indicate that the virus responsible for the death of survivors is a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It appears to be much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More research is needed to better understand its properties and how it ended up on Keeling.

nodes.eventIntro: The fallen fragment of Zephyrus is the epicenter of mass destruction, surrounded by a field of dead, boiled fish bobbing on the disturbed water. It is also in the middle of the anomalous zone.
nodes.eventDescription:
The scouts report malfunctions in their electronic equipment and strange sounds when using communication devices. Each crew member present in the recon craft claims to hear a melody, something from their past. It keeps ringing in their ears, at the back of their mind. Invasive. Persisting. Haunting.
The success of the extraction operation is at risk as long as the anomaly is active. But waiting might not be an option: the fragment is slowly sinking.

actions.description: The scouts believe the sounds lead them on, somewhere. It must be delirium, but… this planet is quite strange. Maybe it warrants an investigation.
actions.resultDescription: The scouts chase the ghostly melody, looping in their heads, taunting, calling. This madness continues for a while until the scouts triumphantly report having found the Source.       The melody... it is now heard on the ship, too. The song Liora loved to listen to. It is in your head, and her voice, bright and worry-free, is so real, you turn around to find her... but she is not there. Then the melody stops. The scouts report they have found a strange artifact. It appears to be the cause of it all.       In the meantime, a large part of the sinking fragment breaks off and sinks into the bottomless dark below. The bridge voice recorder was there, too. And it is gone.

actions.description: STOP THE ANOMALY (THE PLAYER MUST EXTRACT THE ARTIFACT FROM THE ANOMALY
actions.resultDescription: After the anomaly dissipates, the fragment containing the CVR breaks off and disappears in the dark depth of the ocean.

actions.description: The anomaly does not go anywhere, and meanwhile, the debris of Zephyrus is slowly sinking. We should extract the BVR while it is not too late.
actions.resultDescription:
Maddened by the ceaseless melody in their heads, equipped with tools that kept malfunctioning, the scouts have had quite a hard time extracting the target. And when they finally get their hands on the voice recorder, it appears damaged, too.

Not as badly as the previous recorder, though. Some of its data might be saved.

When they finally retrieve the flight recorder, they are happy to leave. In the submarine, they detect something large on their radar. It is rising fast to the surface, in the direction of the ship.

When the drones finally retrieve the flight recorder, the crew is elated to leave the depressing dark of the deep. Before they begin their way back, they detect something large on their radar.

nodes.eventIntro: So, captain… What should we do next?
nodes.eventDescription: At least that explains the time loop. But we need to choose a course of action to break it, preferably with Zephyrus still in one piece.

actions.description: There are other Primordial structures on Keeling. To understand their technology, we must first study it.
actions.resultDescription: We spotted several structures that can be identified as potentially built by the Primordials. They are all in close proximity and potentially reachable by our means of transportation.

actions.description: First, we must find out who destroyed Zephyrus and why.
actions.resultDescription: We have detected several large fragments of Zephyrus nearby. Maybe we could retrieve the Orange box or, at least, examine the debris to learn what type of damage the ship suffered.

actions.description: As we previously found out, the attack could be preceded by sabotage.
actions.resultDescription: We have detected several large fragments of Zephyrus nearby. Maybe we could examine them to learn more about what caused such gruesome damage.

nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventDescription: The complex is built on the floating island. We detect an unknown type of EM-field surrounding the structures.

actions.description: Ask for volunteers. Give them the best protection gear we can provide. We have no time to waste.
actions.resultDescription: Scouts managed to stay there only briefly before their protection began to fail.  They managed to escape, taking with them several slabs of an Eldritium, a rare metal. It probably was mined or refined there. Unfortunately, they also carried radiation sickness.

actions.description: This looks dangerous. We should investigate before putting our scouts at risk.
actions.resultDescription: We still don’t exactly understand what this field is or what its purpose is. But now we know the possible hazards and how to avoid them.

actions.description: Using the gathered information, we can providereliable protection for our scouts.
actions.resultDescription: The scouts still have precious little time to explore the complex. Presumably, it was a refinery for Eldritium, with a significant supply of the material still there. Scouts couldn’t take all, but gathered data about the industrial capacities of the Primordials.

nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventDescription: This looks more like a spacecraft than a marine building. Or even a space station. Crash-landed in these shallows.

actions.description: Despite the sorry state of the structure, we might recover artifacts
actions.resultDescription: Turns out, this was a space station, orbiting the Keeling some centuries, if not millennia ago. Most of the tech here is beyond our understanding, and the in a sorry state because of its age and conditions, but despite that, the scouts retrieved several artifacts. This may be the first step to a real breakthrough.

actions.description: The structure doesn’t look stable. We’ll be putting our crew at risk, sending them without any prior exploration.
actions.resultDescription: Surprisingly, the structure still holds. Now we can clearly tell it was a large orbital station, which, for some reason, left the orbit and landed in the shallows of this archipelago. There is structural damage here and there, but mostly the station is intact. Whatever caused the station to fall didn’t destroy it. We can proceed with the scouting team.

actions.description: Now, when we are sure the place is safe, we can send our scouts.
actions.resultDescription: This was a space station, orbiting the Keeling some centuries, if not millennia ago. Most of the tech here is beyond our understanding, and the in a sorry state because of its age and conditions, but despite that, the scouts retrieved several artifacts. This may be the first step to a real breakthrough.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventDescription: The structure is in very bad shape. Once levitating, it is now half-buried in the soil and heavily damaged.

actions.description: Scanners show no life or energy signatures. The place is dead. We can send the team in.
actions.resultDescription: The place was pillaged a long time ago. Everything was either looted, smashed, or turned to rust & dust. All we can extract from here is some basic materials.

actions.description: We need archeologists here, not looters. We must act carefully.
actions.resultDescription:
The place was pillaged a long time ago. However, the scientists manage to gather intel about the pillagers. This was a native Keeling civilization, primitive but resourceful, capable of recycling the tech, not only extracting precious metals and gems from it. It also seems that they didn’t quite finish their business here. There may be something of value still hidden there.
They went on, but to no avail. Yet just as the search began to look futile, archeologists found a hidden chamber with a strange device, possibly still functional.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventDescription: This fragment has traces of an explosion. A careful study can unveil the details of the attack. However, the fragment is small and badly damaged. We aren’t likely to find any surviving data or gear here.

actions.description: Investigation may take precious time, but it’s the only way to find out how the ship was destroyed.
actions.resultDescription: The investigation showed that the explosion was outward, not inward. Which means that something exploded inside the ship. Whether as the result of sabotage or because of some alien technology, causing some internal devices to explode is yet unclear.

actions.description: Time is of the essence. A quick check will do. We know the weapon was of devastating power, so the knowledge won’t save us from it anyhow.
actions.resultDescription: No luck. The fragment is burned out to ash, leaving nothing of value. We managed to retrieve just a small quantity of rare metals.

actions.description: We can base the investigation on the Orange box data to add more pieces to this puzzle.
actions.resultDescription: The investigation showed that the explosion was outward, not inward. Which means that something exploded inside the ship. The Orange box data shows the critical malfunction in the battery block safety systems in this sector of the ship, seconds before the explosion. Further study is required to clarify the connection between these two occurrences.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: All the points of interest are checked. We can start the research.
nodes.eventDescription: Gathered artifacts and data can tell us more about the Primordials, their motives, and their current state.

actions.description: We only managed to scratch the surface here. More information will be needed to obtain a deeper understanding of the Primordials, but it’s a start.
actions.resultDescription: Despite the first meeting with the Prims, all the structures we’ve found were deserted many centuries ago. What was the creature the Captain spoke to? A ghost? Or maybe they moved on – deeper into the sea perhaps? However, we didn’t find anything that could help us with the riddle of the Prism. We must continue our search.

actions.description: We’ve gathered a lot of data. The Primordials are an advanced and mysterious species, but this research may become a first step in understanding their motives.
actions.resultDescription: We had a first contact, but what was the creature that contacted us? All the structures we explored, even those that were still functioning, were deserted ages ago! Yet, the artifacts we’ve found and the processed data show the possibility of the multidimensional technology being used by the Primordals. However, such tech might require huge amounts of energy. How the Prism is functioning without the potent energy source, and whether there is a limit to its uses, remains unknown.

actions.description: We managed to gather a massive amount of data to research. The main problem now is how to process it.
actions.resultDescription: The data shows that the first contact we had wasn’t a direct contact. At least not as direct as we thought it was. The Primodial wasn’t there in full, and we aren’t even sure that he could be present in a full material form. The one Voss talked to could be either an AI avatar, a transdimensional projection, or even an interactive semi-intelligent recording of the person long gone. The artifacts collected are mostly functional and can be studied to gain a better understanding of the prims’ technology, especially the Prism. What we know now is that the Prism is autonomous and powered by the source beyond our 4 dimensions. All attempts to mess with it will lead to the safety reboot, as well as any serious damage to the ship and crew. We can’t help but wonder: could Zephyrus survive the attack if the Prism were still aboard it?

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventDescription: This fragment is badly damaged, but the damage itself is a bit strange. A closer look shows that the wreck was looted by someone.

actions.description: Have to be quicker next time. Let's retrieve what we can and move on.
actions.resultDescription: The looters were there, and now they are gone. They took almost everything of value. At least all that survived the crash.  All that is left for us is just the basic materials like metal and plastic.

actions.description: Secure the wreck in case the looters are still around and then extract the valuables.
actions.resultDescription:
Whoever did this has some industrial equipment. Not that advanced, but effective. We found some remnants of it: broken parts, exhausted batterys etc. The looters took all they could, even the metal plates that they managed to tear off. They had to have a large vessel to carry all that of the island. Also they picked up all the surviving electronics for some reason.
Were they just occasional marauders or intently covered the tracks of the attack?
One of them lost some kind of decoration, abadge or something. Maybe it will guide us to the marauders in the future.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventDescription: This fragment had sunken by the time we arrived, but scanners detected a strange signal nearby.

actions.description: The waters are shallow here. Maybe we can use divers to reach the Fragment?
actions.resultDescription: No use. Our divers reached the fragment but barely had time to explore it. The local fauna is very aggressive there, so they had to withdraw soon. Still, they managed to recover a data cluster.

actions.description: It might be just our luck, but we should definitely check it.
actions.resultDescription: We found an alien device, damaged by the impact of the fragment’s fall. The device is not functioning, but the examination proves it was a powerful jamming device, perhaps one of those that interfered with the signal from Zephyrus. Hard to tell who built it: the tech is clearly alien and relatively complex.

nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: The R&D formed a task force to study the Explosion
nodes.eventDescription: The data gathered from the damaged Zephyrus fragment could shed some light on the circumstances of the Zephyrus destruction

actions.description: Engineers can research on the Zephyrus design to explain what exactly happened
actions.resultDescription: The report shows that the source of the explosion was the large battery block that feeds the entire Zephyrus section. It is highly unlikely that it exploded due to a critical malfunction. It could be either a concentrated, highly penetrative radiation beam, used as a weapon. Or, it was a planned diversion. Someone either infiltrated the ship or was already aboard to prepare and execute it.

actions.description: Abbadie suggest deeper research of the Orange Box data to match the gathered data on the explosion
actions.resultDescription:
The results show that the malfunction of the battery block, leading to the explosion, started 78 seconds before the explosion. This makes the sabotage theory highly improbable, for in such a short time, the saboteur couldn’t possibly escape the explosion, not to say reach the escape pods. It could have been the result of the outer action, most likely the penetrative radiation, strong enough to break through the Zephyrus’s shields.
Yet one group of researchers states that the earlier records contain data on the safety system breach in this sector, which suggests the sabotage was a planned-ahead action.
This could mean that the saboteur left Zephyrus. Perhaps even as a part of the Behemoth crew.

lines.text: Commander, the beacon frequency matches pre-collapse naval telemetry. Proceed with caution.
Captain, we've located the lifeboat within comm link reach.
Finally... let me speak to them.
This is Elias Voss, captain of BCEV-07M. Can someone hear me?
Oh, thank goodness... We contracted something on that island. It hurts so much.
The lifepod's log states there was a child on board...
I wasn't the only parent back on Zephyrus. It means nothing.
Listen... is it true that there is a child with you?
Yes, I've got my daughter here.
That's the thing—it shouldn't have happened! The virus couldn't have bypassed their suits.
So we're not going to have our brains bleed out of our eyes. That's nice.
I believe it was a bioweapon.
Captain, we got the orange box! But... it doesn't have anything about the last ten minutes.
Inside job?
I can't see how an outside force could have paralyzed Zephyrus's entire nervous system.
Captain, the transmitter has detected a signal awfully similar to the frequency our escape shuttles and pods use.
We must check it out then. Add its location to the navigation panel.
Right away!
And, Captain?
What?
I just wanted to say, you know, you shouldn't lose hope just yet.
Stop. That's enough.
Why? Zephyrus had enough pods for mass evacuation.
I'm afraid to get my hopes up...
...afraid to feel the heartbreak again...
...losing her again and again, each time I open the escape pod and she's not there...
It's easier to accept, just in case.
I must say I'm surprised by your decision. I thought you would make us overturn every slab of metal from Zephyrus, just to be sure.
And I am not the only one. Many are... disappointed.
And what about you? Disappointed, as well?
I... I understand your point of view. But are you yourself on board with what you are doing?
We must know what happened to Zephyrus. If we want to survive.
I can see there's something else you're not saying.
It's just...
I'm done lying to myself.
Liora couldn't have reached the emergency bay in time. Every upturned slab, every lifepod without her inside would...
...would kill me.
No point in chasing ghosts. No, I want to know what happened and if there is someone — keyword, someone — responsible for this.
The lifepod's log states there was a child on board...
I wasn't the only parent back on Zephyrus. It means nothing.
I see it in your eyes: it means a lot.

Yes. 

I'm terrified.
Captain, we've got an incoming transmission from the lifeboat.
Finally... let me speak to them. This is Elias Voss, the captain of BCEV-07M, speaking. Can someone hear me?
Is... is this real? Or am I... imagining this?
I reassure you, this is quite true. We've come to help you.
Oh, thank goodness.
Listen... is it true that then is a child with you?
Survivor (generic icon): Yes, I've got my daughter here.
Your daughter? I... I see.
Um, listen, you have doctors on the ship, right?
Is someone hurt?
We think we've... um, contracted something on that island. We're not feeling too well. Please, help us. It hurts so much.
Let's stay focused on the pod. The Reckon Craft cargo space is limited and we will need all the gear we can get.
Contact with Zephyrus is lost, Captain. Visual analysis suggests it has been destroyed. Calculating potential casualties...
With all likelihood, there is little to no chance of survivors.
No...
No, it... it can't be...
Captain, per protocol, you are now in charge of the entire mission.
Captain?
Just...
Just give a moment...
Unfortunately, this is an emergency, and therefore, not an appropriate time for a ‘moment.’
Now, shall we review all the possible courses of action available?
I'm ready when you are.
Captain, I have completed my analysis and added the expected location of the flight recorder to the navigation panel.
Thank you, M.
I also wanted to discuss the recent decrease in crew morale. An unhappy crew leads to complications. Did you consider giving a motivational speech?
To give a good speech, one must believe in what gospels he's spewing. Me? I don't know that I do. Besides, I hate giving speeches. I'm the man of action, preferring the results to speak for myself.
No speech? Alright.
You must try to meet some of their needs then: to reinforce their sense of security.
I'll keep it in mind.
Captain, I've established the location of the bridge voice recorder. Adding it to your navigation panel!
Thanks, M.
Captain, with all due respect, but it is not too late to turn back and start looking for the survivors.
Believe me, I do not forget, not for a moment, about those people. But first, we must—
Why?! What does it change? Help me understand, ‘cause I can't see why we would choose an obituary over people's lives!

I'm doing it for the crew! Zephyrus traversed lightyears of void, passed asteroid fields, escaped black holes, all to be annihilated just outside this Primordial planet... If there's someone or something responsible for what happened... we must know.
What can just one ship do?
We'll find the way. End of the discussion.
Tuuli, tell me you can restore some of the data from the recorder.
Oh, I can... just not about the last hours of Zephyrus. That information is gone for good.
Was it our fault?
I can't tell. The casing was ruptured. The contents damaged. Could've happened at various points of its fall.
Is there anything... anything at all that we can learn?
Only that there was nothing abnormal in the ship's systems two days before. If it were a malfunction, it must've manifested itself today.
